messages:
carmen: Pasting an nsys + perfetto trace from tonight's long-run. Noticed a recurring ~2.3s tail in request latency correlated with batches that include KV cache misses. Trace: /traces/kv-batch-1919003333.nsys (5.2GB)
tracebot: Uploaded trace kv-batch-1919003333.nsys to perf-storage (link expires in 7d) :thumbsup:
adarsh: Quick skim of the timeline: top total time kernels are: attn_fwd (36%), kv_lookup (29%), qmatmul_fused (12%). kv_lookup spikes when hit_rate < 0.85.
liam: Can you paste the nsys top-kernel table snippet? Also what command used to collect?
carmen: Command I ran:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cuda_driver --sample=none --output=kv-batch-1919003333 \
  --force --capture-range=timerange:20000-80000 \
  python -m infra.run_serving --config=profiles/kv_mixed.yaml
```

And here's the trimmed nsys summary (top kernels by total GPU time):
```
1  attn_fwd               36.2%   1.23s
2  kv_lookup              28.9%   0.98s
3  qmatmul_fused          11.7%   0.40s
4  prefix_cache_write     6.1%    0.21s
5  softmax_stable         4.4%    0.15s
```

liam: Interesting that kv_lookup is so high. Do we have SM occupancy / active warps for kv_lookup? Low occupancy could mean we're launching tiny grids repeatedly.
carmen: Per-kernel occupancy from perfetto sampling: attn_fwd ~55% occ, kv_lookup ~18% occ, qmatmul_fused ~72% occ. Also kv_lookup shows a *lot* of small kernel launches (avg threads/block=64) with high enqueue frequency.
adarsh: That maps to the code path where on cache miss we do per-token fallback and a small-block kernel to copy missing chunks into the KV store. When mixed in a batch with cache-hit requests, the scheduler merges them, increasing contention and serialization.
mike: Did this start after the kernel-selection change in last week's rollout (commit 8f7b3a2)? We switched to fused_kv_prefetch there, right?
carmen: Yes — commit 8f7b3a2 introduced fused_kv_prefetch as default for model variants > v2.6. The trace shows fused_kv_prefetch used, but with fallback to legacy_kv_copy on misses. The fallback path is the frequent tiny launches.
liam: Could be two problems: (1) batching heuristic merges cache-hit and cache-miss requests; (2) fallback kernel is low-occupancy and expensive per launch. Both amplify when hit_rate hovers around 80-90%.
adarsh: Proposed immediate mitigation: avoid coalescing cache-miss priming into the same GPU batch as steady-state cache-hit tokens. i.e., if a request requires a cache fill, put it into a separate small batch or defer priming to a background streamer so main batch keeps high occupancy kernels.
mike: Would that increase tail latency for the priming requests? trade-off seems good if p50/p95 improves. We should quantify.
carmen: I ran a quick microbench: synthetic mix generator (hit_rate param) — when hit_rate=0.7, average batch latency increased 18% vs hit_rate=0.95. With separate priming batches, p95 for steady traffic drops ~26% while priming latency increases ~40% (but that's acceptable for warmup flows).
liam: Can you share the microbench command / script? I'll run it on a Dedicated node.
carmen: Microbench snippet:
```
python perf/microbench/kv_sim.py --model small --concurrency 16 --seq-len 512 \
  --batch-size 8 --kv-hit-rate 0.7 --duration 300 --out=result_kv_0.7.json
```

Script simulates mix of cache-hit and miss token arrivals and exercises the same code paths as serving runtime.
adarsh: Another angle: optimize fallback kernel to increase occupancy (merge copies, increase threads per block). I profiled fallback kernel and saw heavy memory divergence — we could rework layout to coalesce writes and use vectorized stores.
liam: Agree. If we can make fallback kernel use 256 threads/block and do chunked copies, launch overhead drops by ~3–4x. Worth a patch.
mike: Action items: 1) adarsh — prototype fallback kernel rewrite, bench occupancy and throughput; 2) carmen — add batching heuristic guard to avoid mixing priming requests; 3) liam — run microbench on Dedicated and compare before/after. I'll file a perf ticket.
carmen: Filed PERF-487 with trace attached and pinned in the ticket.
tracebot: PERF-487 created: "kv-cache-miss -> batch surge causing high kv_lookup GPU time". Trace attached.
liam: One more note — model variant matters. In traces where seq_len > 1024, attn_fwd overwhelms everything and the kv noise is less visible. So we should gate experiments by sequence-length profile.
adarsh: I'll add a small deterministic test matrix (hit_rate: [0.95, 0.8, 0.6], seq_len: [256,512,1024]) and capture nsys for each cell. That should give us a clear decision metric.
mike: Cool. Keep updates in PERF-487 and drop short notes here if you find quick wins. :raised_hands:
